_comment: Trust policy for edullm-reservoir-publish — WHO may become this role.
`ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` only, identical in shape to 08-reservoir-ingest-trust-policy.json and
to the validator's. AWS Batch runs containers as ECS tasks, so that principal is what a running
job needs; no human session and no EC2 instance can assume it.
This matters more for this role than for the builder. The intern role in this account carries
AdministratorAccess, so IAM is not what keeps a human out of the pipeline's identities — this
trust policy is. And this is the one reservoir role permitted to write `dataset.json` and
`manifest.json`, i.e. the one whose credentials could fire the validator. Keeping it
unassumable from a session is what makes 'publishing happens only through a Batch job' a
Deliberately NO `Condition` block, for the reason recorded on the ingest role: Batch does not
populate `aws:SourceArn` on the ECS task-assume call the way one would expect, so a SourceArn
condition scoping this to one job queue evaluates false and every job fails to start with an
unhelpful credential error. The blast radius is bounded by the permission policy
(09-reservoir-publish-policy.json), which Denies all writes to edullm-data.
